title: CLAY COUNTY TAX SALE
full_story:
Clay County, as Trustee, has completed their tax deed proceedings on real estate properties and mobile homes.  The County, as Trustee, will now offer for sale the real estate and mobile homes obtained to the public through a sealed bid auction.

They will offer approximately 9 real estate items 2 mobile home items and 1 mineral rights item through a sealed bid auction sale.  All sealed written bids must be in the Clay County Treasurer’s Office located in the Clay County Courthouse, at 111 Chestnut Street, in Louisville, no later than the close of business on October 2nd.  All online bids must be submitted via www. iltaxsalebids.com no later than the close of business on October 2nd.

The sale of these lots and mobile homes should be a major benefit to both the Taxing Districts and the neighboring property owners.  This sale will place the real estate and mobile homes into the hands of individuals who have an interest in owning them.  The County, as Trustee, hopes that these new owners will both maintain the property and the mobile homes and keep the taxes paid.  By eliminating abandoned properties, the appearance of the neighborhood should improve, and the value of adjoining properties should increase.

The required minimum bid on real estate is $844.00, and on mobile homes is $915.00.  All items will be sold to the highest sealed bid received on or before October 2nd.  Complete bidder’s packets and sale catalogs are now available at the Clay County Treasurer’s Office or online at www. iltaxsale.com.

For further sale information, contact the Auction Sale Department of the Clay County Tax Agent’s Office.  The telephone number is 1-800-248-2850 or 618-656-5744 or visit us at www.iltaxsale.com.  Office hours are 8:00 am and 5:00 pm Monday through Fridays.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corp, as administrator of the Energy Assistance Program in the counties of Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie and Shelby announced that funds are available to assist income-eligible households with their natural gas, propane and/or electric bills and furnace assistance for inoperable heating systems.

The program will begin taking applications on October 1st, for older adults, age 60 and over, individuals with a disability, families with children age 5 years and under, and households that are disconnected from their utilities, have a disconnection notice or have less than 25% in their propane tank.  All other income eligible households can start applying November 2nd.

Applications will be taken on a first-come, first-served basis through August 13th, of 2027, or until funding is exhausted.  Households that receive a one-time benefit may return during the program year for a Reconnection Assistance or Furnace Assistance benefits, if needed.

The program has expanded eligibility this year.  Households that are customers of Ameren Illinois, Liberty Utilities, City of Flora, Village of Louisville, Village of Clay City or Shelby Electric must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.

The monthly income guidelines are as follows, one person can make up to $3,990, two people can make up to $5,410, three people can make up to $6,830, and four people can make up to $8,250.

Households that are customers of all other utilities/energy vendors must be at or below 60% of the State Median Income to receive a benefit from LIHEAP.  The income guidelines for that are as follows, one person can make up to $3,441, two people can make up to $4,500, three people can make up to $5,558, and four people can make up to $6,617.

Go to www.cefseoc.org or liheapillinois.com for the income limits for households with 5 members and more.

The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) provides one-time benefits to income eligible homeowners and renters to help with energy bills and for reconnection of energy service.

The following documentation is required for all applications; Proof of gross income from all household members for the prior 30-day period beginning with the date of application.  For all customers new to LIHEAP, and/or for new household members of previous customers, proof of Social Security numbers (SSN) for all household members.  Individuals without an SSN or Individual Taxpayer Identification Number (ITIN) can still apply and CEFS Outreach offices will advise accordingly.  A copy of current heat and electric bills issued within the last 30 days.  Cash assistance is available for renters who can provide a copy of their lease/rental agreement showing their heating costs are included in the rent.  Other documents may be needed based on your household situation.  If you have questions regarding this, please call the office.

Starting on September 21st appointments can be made by contacting the CEFS Clay County Outreach office at 835 West North Street in Flora the phone number is 618-662-4024.  The office is open Monday through Friday 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

In order that no one is denied the opportunity to make an application we will continue to take applications in person or by phone.  Required documentation can be submitted in-person, mail or electronically.  If you require any special accommodation, please contact the local CEFS Outreach office in your county to arrange.

Income eligible LIHEAP customers of Ameren Illinois will receive a monthly discount on their natural and/or electric bill through the Low-Income Discount Rates.  Visit powerbilldiscount.com to know more details.

title: FIRE IN DOWNTOWN DU QUOIN
full_story:
A 5-alarm fire rapidly spread through downtown Du Quoin Wednesday afternoon, consuming Home Lumber Company and spreading to nearby businesses.  Mayor Josh Downs said on Facebook “Please avoid downtown Du Quoin until otherwise notified, give our first responders the room to do their job. Pray for everyone impacted!”

The Franklin County Office of Emergency Management and Communications said the Du Quoin Fire Department was supported by MABAS Division 68, which provided dispatch, communications and additional emergency resources. OEMC also deployed its Special Operations Drone Team to assist incident command.  At least 30 fire departments reportedly responded to the scene.

Main Street was closed, and officials warned of possible low water pressure, power outages and interruptions to CN and Amtrak rail service.  The cause, injury information and full extent of the damage had not been released.

title: MEASLES OUTBREAK
full_story:
An outbreak of measles is officially confirmed in Douglas County.

The Illinois Department of Public Health said the outbreak includes at least four confirmed, linked cases.  Health officials are working with the Douglas County Health Department to identify anyone who was exposed and offer vaccination to those in the community, especially those at high risk.

“Illinois is fortunate to have high vaccination rates overall that protect most Illinois residents from measles,” said IDPH Director Dr. Sameer Vohra.  “However, there are still areas across the state with lower vaccination rates where people are at high risk.  With almost 3,000 cases in the US so far this year, IDPH has been preparing and works closely with local public health and health care partners on strategies to reduce spread and minimize outbreaks.  IDPH continues to urge clinicians to be attentive to pre-travel vaccination needs and consider a measles diagnosis in patients with consistent symptoms and alert their local health department immediately if they suspect a case.”

Measles was declared eliminated in the US in 2000, but it is seeing a resurgence in recent years as immunization rates have dropped.  It is a highly contagious disease caused by a virus and is spread through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

“The key to preventing measles is the highly effective measles/mumps/rubella (MMR) vaccine.  Two doses of measles vaccine are 97% effective in preventing measles,” Dr. Vohra added.  “I recommend that our Illinois residents make sure that they and their family members are up to date on the MMR vaccine and all other age-appropriate immunizations.”

Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) can be administered to unvaccinated people six months and older who are exposed to measles, but they must receive the shot within 72 hours of first exposure.  In addition, an injection known as immune globulin can be provided to high-risk individuals who cannot receive the measles vaccine or who missed the 72-hour window, including infants, pregnant persons, or people who are immunocompromised.

title: ISP LABOR DAY CAMPAIGN
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation, Illinois State Police and law enforcement agencies throughout the state are reminding the public to drive responsibly by ramping up efforts to get impaired drivers off the roads during Labor Day holiday travel.

“There’s no excuse for driving impaired, period,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering at IDOT.  “The consequences of driving impaired could be costly and deadly.  Remember, driving under the influence is ‘Not a Game.’”

During the Labor Day safety campaign, which runs through September 8th, ISP, local police and sheriff’s departments are reminding the public that driving under the influence can come with real-life, sobering consequences.

“Holiday weekends are busy travel weekends.  ISP troopers will be on the roads looking for impaired drivers,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Chris Owen.  “Whether alcohol or drugs, driving impaired puts your life and the lives of others at risk.  If you’re driving, plan ahead and stay safe.”

According to IDOT data, last Labor Day weekend from 6 pm Friday, August 29th, to 11:59 pm Monday, September 1st, there were nine fatalities on Illinois roads.  Three of the nine fatal crashes were alcohol-related, resulting in three of the nine fatalities.

To help make your Labor Day weekend a safe one, remember these important tips, if you’re planning to use cannabis or alcohol, give your keys to a sober driver or call a taxi or rideshare service.  If you see or suspect an impaired driver, contact law enforcement.  Remind your friends to never get in a vehicle with an impaired driver.  If you have a friend who is about to drive while impaired, take their keys away and help them get home safely. Don’t worry about offending them, you might be saving a life.

In addition to the heightened focus on impaired driving, the campaign also reinforces the importance of seat belt use, adherence to the speed limit and other traffic laws.  Seat belt laws will be enforced as part of the national “Click It or Ticket” and “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” programs, which are made possible by federal funds administered by IDOT and coincide with the department’s comprehensive multimedia campaign, “It’s Not a Game.”

title: 2026 ILLINOIS PRODUCT EXPO
full_story:
The Du Quoin State Fair celebrates Illinois agriculture, the state’s number one industry, and there’s no better way to experience it than with a visit to the 2026 Illinois Product Expo.

“Consumers are increasingly interested in where their food comes from, and the Illinois Product Expo is a great way to connect buyers with local farmers and producers,” said Jerry Costello II, Director of the Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA).  “With demand for locally grown products on the rise, we’re excited to showcase the best of Illinois agriculture at the Du Quoin State Fair.”

The Illinois Product Expo, located in the Expo Hall, will be open the second weekend of the Du Quoin State Fair.  Shop for local products Friday, September 4th from 5 to 9 pm; Saturday, September 5th from 9 am to 8 pm; and Sunday, September 6th from 11 am to 5 pm.

Vendors will be offering samples and selling seasonings, jellies and jams, honey, freeze dried candy, salsa, coffee, herbal tea, soaps, lip balm, birdhouses, wood and gourd crafts, candles and much more.  In addition, several Illinois wineries will offer wine tasting.

“The Illinois Product Expo in Du Quoin is one of my favorite opportunities to celebrate the incredible flavors of Southern Illinois,” said Kayla Graven, IDOA Domestic Marketing Manager.  “It’s a chance for people to sample outstanding local products and support the companies that make Illinois so vibrant.  We’re proud to showcase the creativity and quality of the businesses.”

The Du Quoin State Fair runs through September 7th.  Admission to the fair is free.  Please visit dsf.illinois.gov for additional information including seasonal parking and handicap parking details.
